environment: Disposable Ubuntu 24.04 CI; loopback TLS, temporary Unix sockets, unprivileged controller fixture and opt-in root fixture with forked UID 991/992/994 processes
qualifiedScope: Gateway UID 992 forwards an actual certificate-verified TLS 1.3 HTTP request over a protected Unix socket to a distinct controller UID 991 using production proxy and peer-context handlers.
Public forwarding assertions are replaced at the private boundary; the distinct controller sees only the qualified synthetic client address and trusted HTTPS context.
TLS 1.2 handshake, untrusted certificate root, mismatched certificate server name and foreign HTTP Host cases refuse.
Foreign client UID 994 is refused; relabeling the listener socket to an expected owner UID 990 does not bypass the serving-kernel-peer pin to UID 991.

A separate unprivileged same-UID fixture constructs the production HTTPS controller and checks health, unauthenticated Files refusal, seeded Files-only access and device-administration refusal through real verified TLS and the production proxy.
That controller fixture marks its seeded device revoked and verifies that the same cookie receives HTTP 401 while reusing the already-established client TLS connection.
Production controller responses retain HSTS and no-store headers.
Separate root file-admission tests refuse protected-file ownership/link/mode/ACL violations; this does not combine protected certificate-file loading with the real-TLS peer fixture.
limitations: Both TLS fixtures substitute a synthetic tailnet RemoteAddr for real loopback TCP addresses; no Tailscale enrollment, routing, device allowlist or overlay ACL is qualified.
TLS certificates are trusted test fixtures, not production issuance, protected certificate-file rotation or actual gateway-executable startup.
Distinct-UID transport uses a minimal controller handler; production controller authorization uses a same-UID fixture. These are separate checks rather than combined installed service confinement.

Sessions are seeded and revocation updates the fixture database directly; no WebAuthn enrollment, owner approval flow, active download/AI stream termination or physical-device propagation is qualified.
No installed systemd confinement, certificate rotation, physical-host operation, independent security review or complete release qualification.
